The prize is a program they already run

Every day of this trip happens somewhere Ole Smoky owns.

You sleep in Gatlinburg and spend the days at the distilleries. Nobody can rent a cabin and copy that.

The Hooch Hop is Ole Smoky’s own scavenger hunt across three East Tennessee distilleries. Buy something at each one, collect three stamps, walk out with the shirt. It’s been running since 2022 and it works. It’s also a paper passport stamped at a register, so whoever finishes it walks out with no name attached to any of it. The Golden Jar is that same walk, paid for, and this time it arrives with an identity.

The Hop is real. The prize is not, yet. Visitor counts are Ole Smoky’s own. Open for what is verified and what still needs clearing.

The Hooch Hop is a real Ole Smoky program, live on their location pages today, and it does carry a purchase requirement at each stop.

The visitor figures are Ole Smoky’s own 2023 reporting, measured by their on-premise traffic counters and published in February 2024. The most visited distillery claim is the company’s own rather than an audited one, which is worth knowing before anybody repeats it.

The prize weekend, the amounts and the entry mechanics on this page are an illustrative concept. Official rules and legal review come before any of it runs.

Photography is reference material for this concept only: The Barn courtesy of BarberMcMurry Architects project photography, cabin imagery via Cabins For You, jars via SmokyMountains.com. Licensing would be cleared before publication.

Or don’t wait at all

Skip the drawing. Spend the points.

One name gets pulled a week, so most people don’t win. That’s a strange way to thank somebody for showing up. So the points are the other door. Earn them on things you were going to do anyway, and take the shirt without ever being drawn.

Points are earned on actions and spent on merchandise. They are never earned on the purchase of whiskey and they never redeem for it, which is what keeps this legal in every state including the strict ones.

      Activity

        Put Your Name In The Jar is a campaign concept and portfolio work sample created by Nathan J. Song for the Ole Smoky Distillery CRM Director role. It is not affiliated with, sponsored by, or endorsed by Ole Smoky Distillery.

        No live drawing is being run on this page and no entry is being collected. The Smoky Mountain Takeover, the runner-up kits, the name counter, the 2,500 points, the $15 code and every figure in the forecast are proposed, illustrative, and modeled. Product names, apparel, venues and the Hooch Hop are drawn from public sources including olesmoky.com. Merchandise imagery is official Ole Smoky imagery used as visual reference for a concept.

        Official rules summary

        This is a concept work sample. Nothing here is live. The summary shows the structure a real drawing needs, and it would go to counsel before anything launched.

        Sponsor
        Shown here as Ole Smoky Distillery for the purposes of the concept. No sponsorship exists.
        Eligibility
        Legal residents of eligible states, 21 or over at entry. Eligible states are set per drawing by counsel rather than fixed in the page, because no two spirits promotions run the same list. Employees and representatives of alcohol wholesalers and retailers are excluded, and the account carries a flag so the exclusion happens at the draw rather than on the honor system.
        No purchase necessary
        A free entry is available every day on the main screen, in the same number of taps as any other route, writing to the same jar with the same weight.
        Entry period
        Monthly. Entries close when the timer closes and the next period opens the same day.
        Prize
        One name per weekly period, and one grand prize a month. Four runner-up kits, each one shirt and one cooler bag. One Golden Jar winner receives the Smoky Mountain Takeover, a trip with an illustrative retail value of $5,000. Alcohol is not part of any prize, because alcohol cannot lawfully be a prize; the distillery tasting is an experience at a licensed venue and any guest must also be 21 or over.
        Registration and bonding
        The weekly prize pool crosses the New York and Florida $5,000 registration thresholds, so filing and bonding lead time (30 days and 7 days) sits on the launch calendar rather than being discovered after. Eligible states remain a per-drawing decision made with counsel.
        Odds
        Determined by the number of eligible entries received.
        Winner selection and notification
        Random draw from all eligible entries. Winners notified by email, with a signed declaration and proof of age before anything ships.
        Referral entries
        One additional entry per completed friend entry, capped at three per calendar month, credited only when that person finishes registration and confirms 21 or over. Duplicates across email, phone and address are removed.
        Points and codes
        Jar Points are earned on actions and redeem for merchandise only, and a member may redeem for a shirt without ever entering the drawing. They are never earned on the purchase of alcohol and never redeem for it. The $15 code applies to merchandise.
        Privacy
        Entry data would be held under a published privacy notice, with consent recorded per channel and a working opt out on every message.
